title: Standby bailout bridge: telemetry-snooze and rollbackable restore
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Context and motivation: We observed a cascading tenant impact during a recent regional ingress surge where standby routes were promoted prematurely and telemetry floods caused the circuit controller to rapidly flip eviction decisions. This PR adds a lightweight 'standby bailout bridge' that acts as a short-lived intermediary when promoting standby routes. The bridge introduces a telemetry-snooze window (configurable) during which aggressive telemetry spikes are sampled and smoothed, preventing immediate eviction/restore thrash and enabling a rollbackable restore path if downstream SLOs regress. This change is an emergency/near-term stability improvement that complements longer-term scheduling work (ENG-1829).

What this PR changes (high level):
- introduce service/standby_bailout.go: new coordinator that tracks standby promotions and opens a telemetry-snooze window for a candidate route
- add rollbackable restore token in route state to support safe undo of promotions when SLO regressions are detected
- adapt circuit-controller to consult bailout coordinator before committing hard evictions or permanent restores
- lightweight sampling telemetry path: telemetry/sampler.go with region-scoped dampening for noisy metrics
- admin flags and toggle: --standby-bailout-enabled, --bailout-snooze-ms, and per-tenant opt-out
- tests and integration harness updates covering rollback scenarios and telemetry spike simulation

Commits (summary):
- e2a1f22: initial coordinator implementation and API surface
- 6b4c8d3: integrate coordinator with circuit-controller and introduce rollback token
- 8f0b6a1: add telemetry sampler and unit tests simulating spike windows
- bf13d90: add admin flags, docs, and telemetry metric names
- c3d2e44: fix race condition in promotion path observed in integration run

Files/areas touched (high level):
- serving/runtime/circuit-controller.go (small refactor and new consult hook)
- serving/runtime/standby_bailout.go (new)
- telemetry/sampler.go (new)
- api/flags.go (admin flags)
- tests/integration/standby_bailout_test.go (new integration tests)
- docs/operational/standby-bailout.md (operator-facing docs)

Testing and CI: Unit test suite passed locally; CI initially reported a flaky integration failure (integration/standby_bailout_test timed out on first run). Reran the integration job which passed on the second try. CI summary: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), integration-tests (pass after rerun), lint (pass). Telemetry smoke test added to integration harness to assert no metric cardinality explosion.

Review thread (highlights):
- Liam Chen (reviewer): "This looks sound; two concerns: 1) the telemetry-snooze default must be conservative to avoid hiding real regressions, 2) need a clear operator-visible metric for number of rollbacks to avoid silent oscillation." Author response: "Agreed. Default set to 5000ms in this PR; added metric redwood.standby_bailout.rollbacks and an alert suggestion in docs."
- Priya Kapoor (SRE): "Please ensure per-tenant opt-out is enforced at admission to avoid surprising tenants with different behaviour." Author response: "Added per-tenant opt-out gate at route admission and a unit test exercising opt-out."
- Marco Ruiz (perf): "Race seen in promotion path on load testing; recommend deferring lock release until rollback token is persisted." Author response: "Fixed in c3d2e44; added comment and simplified lock handoff to avoid races."
- External QA (comment): "Observed a slight increase in median promotion latency (~6ms) when bailout is enabled under microbenchmarks — acceptable tradeoff but documented." Author response: "Documented expected latency increase and added admin toggle for canarying."

Risk and rollout plan: This is a targeted hotfix intended for quick rollout to reduce regional thrash. Rollout steps:
1) Enable feature behind admin flag on staging and run the new integration harness for 24h traffic replay.
2) Canary enable on 10% of traffic in one region for 2 hours while monitoring redwood.slo.latency and redwood.standby_bailout.rollbacks.
3) Increase to 50% if no SLO regressions; full rollout thereafter. A rollback path exists: disabling the admin flag will immediately bypass the coordinator for future promotions, and route state tokens make previously-promoted routes eligible for a fast revert path.

Operational notes and metrics: Added the following telemetry names and recommended alerts in docs: redwood.standby_bailout.promotions, redwood.standby_bailout.rollbacks, redwood.standby_bailout.snooze_count, redwood.standby_bailout.snooze_duration_ms (histogram). Suggested alert: >3 rollbacks in 10min for a region => pause rollout and investigate.

Release notes (for changelog): "Hotfix: add standby bailout bridge to smooth standby route promotions and provide rollbackable restores to reduce regional eviction/restore thrash under telemetry spikes. Disabled by default; enable via --standby-bailout-enabled."

Merge outcome: After approvals from Liam Chen and Priya Kapoor and green CI (integration rerun), PR was rebased and merged. Merge method: rebase. Post-merge: a follow-up patch will add a canary config in the cluster-config repo and a Linear task was created to track longer-term scheduler work (ENG-1834).

Follow-ups and TODOs: 1) Add end-to-end canary configuration in infra (Linear: ENG-1832), 2) add more robust sampling heuristics tuned via historical telemetry (SRE-74), 3) review interplay with Dedicated eviction policies (ENG-1834).

Notes on uniqueness: This approach prefers a brief intermediary 'bridge' that allows controlled promotion with an explicit short-lived rollback token rather than immediate permanent state transitions. It is intentionally conservative — aims to reduce thrash without masking real SLO regressions; telemetry counters and an operator-facing opt-out are included to preserve visibility and control.
